title: Lace fingerless mitts in DK wool
subtitle: Simple eyelet lace panel on the back of the hand, afterthought thumb.
excerpt: Fingerless mitts with a four-stitch eyelet lace column running up the back of the hand. DK weight, worked in the round, afterthought thumb. Three sizes for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Knitter, 7th series (1880s), §Lace mittens. Eyelet-panel fingerless mitts appear in Weldon's and in Beeton's Book of Needlework (1870), §Lace-work mittens. Both are out of UK and EU copyright.

knitting.gaugeText: 22 sts × 30 rounds = 10 × 10 cm in stocking stitch on 3.75 mm needles, blocked.
knitting.finishedSizeText: Hand circumference 18 (20, 22) cm with 1 to 2 cm negative ease.

glossaryTerms.definition: An increase and the basis of lace. The yarn is brought over the needle to create a new loop, which becomes a stitch on the next round. Worked alongside a decrease, a yarn over creates an eyelet hole without changing the stitch count.

A thumb opening made by working the thumb stitches in waste yarn during the hand, then returning to them after the hand is complete. The waste yarn is removed to reveal live stitches which are picked up and worked as the thumb.
A method for knitting small circumferences in the round on one long circular needle. The cable is pulled into a loop at the midpoint so each half of the stitches sits on its own needle tip.

content.text: Fingerless mitts with a simple eyelet lace column on the back of the hand, sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.
These are worked in the round using
magic loop
on a long circular. The lace pattern is an 8-round repeat of
yarn over
eyelets flanked by k2tog. On the remaining stitches the fabric is 1×1 rib. The thumb uses the
afterthought thumb
method, placed on the palm side so the lace column is uninterrupted. Budget about 85 g (190 m / 210 yards) of DK wool.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.substitutions: A smooth-plied DK works best for lace; fuzzy fibres (mohair blends) obscure the eyelet holes.

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 3.75 mm (UK 9 / US 5) circular needle, at least 80 cm cable

items.name: Stitch markers
items.qty: 3: 1 for beginning of round, 2 to flank the lace panel

items.name: Waste yarn
items.qty: About 30 cm of smooth contrasting yarn for the thumb

content.text: Gauge

22 stitches and 30 rounds to 10 cm over stocking stitch on 3.75 mm needles, blocked. The eyelet panel is 12 stitches wide. Its width in the finished mitt is set by the rib gauge on either side, not the lace gauge.
Lace pattern (12-stitch panel)

items.name: Round 4 (eyelet round)
items.qty: k2tog, yo, k2, k2tog, yo, k2, k2tog, yo, k2. Stitch count unchanged: each k2tog is paired with a yo.

items.name: Round 8 (eyelet round)
items.qty: k2, k2tog, yo, k2, k2tog, yo, k2, k2tog, yo. Stitch count unchanged.

content.text: Stitches used

items.name: yo
items.qty: yarn over (an increase that creates an eyelet)

content.text: Pattern
Before you cast on, circle your size. Every stitch count and measurement reads S (M, L) for hand circumferences 18 (20, 22) cm.
Cast on and cuff
Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 36 (40, 44) stitches. Join to work in the round. Work 1×1 rib (k1, p1 every round) for 20 (22, 24) rounds.
Set up the lace panel
The beginning of the round is at the palm. Work across 12 (14, 16) palm stitches in 1×1 rib, PM, work the 12 lace panel stitches, PM, continue in 1×1 rib to end.
Hand and thumb marker

Work 8 (10, 10) rounds in pattern. On the next round, place the thumb marker on the palm: work 5 (6, 7) palm rib stitches, knit 7 (8, 9) stitches with waste yarn, slip back and knit with main yarn, continue in pattern to end. Continue in pattern for 16 (18, 20) more rounds.
Finger edge
Work 6 rounds of 1×1 rib across all stitches (replacing the lace panel with rib) for a neat edge. Bind off in 1×1 rib.
Thumb
Remove waste yarn and pick up 7 (8, 9) stitches above and below the gap. Total: 14 (16, 18) thumb stitches. Work 10 (12, 12) rounds of 1×1 rib. Bind off in rib.
Common faults

Stitch count increases after the eyelet round: a yarn over was worked without its paired k2tog. Each yarn over in rounds 4 and 8 must be accompanied by a k2tog. Count 12 stitches in the panel at the end of every eyelet round.
Eyelets not visible after blocking: the yarn chosen is too textured (halo or boucle). Use a smooth, tightly plied DK for the best eyelet definition.
Finishing
Weave in all tails on the wrong side. Block by soaking in cool water, then pin the lace panel flat and allow to dry completely. The eyelets open up noticeably after wet-blocking.
Care
Hand wash in cool water. Block flat each time for best eyelet definition.
What to try next
A leaf motif of four stitches (ssk, yo, yo, k2tog) in the centre of the panel is a natural next step. It adds a decrease at each side of the leaf and looks much harder to knit than it is.
